LESSON: METALS AND ALLOYS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds
Topic 1.2: Metals and Alloys

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Metals and Alloys. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are alloys important in day-to- day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the physical properties of metals
2. describe the composition of alloys
3. identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life
4. explain the effects of rusting of metals
5. appreciate the importance of common alloys in day-to-day life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: METALS AND ALLOYS
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Metals and Alloys helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: METALS AND ALLOYS
Study Metals and Alloys like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the physical properties of metals

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the physical properties of metals. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the physical properties of metals.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Metals and Alloys” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the physical properties of metals. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the composition of alloys

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the composition of alloys. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the composition of alloys.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Metals and Alloys matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the composition of alloys. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Metals and Alloys this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Explain the effects of rusting of metals

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the effects of rusting of metals. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the effects of rusting of metals.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Metals and Alloys” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the effects of rusting of metals. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Appreciate the importance of common alloys in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of common alloys in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of common alloys in day-to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Metals and Alloys matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of common alloys in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Metals and Alloys is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Metals and Alloys” around your school. (skill: describe the physical properties of metals)

Example 2: Say why Metals and Alloys matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe the composition of alloys)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Metals and Alloys this week. (skill: identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Metals and Alloys” around your school. (skill: explain the effects of rusting of metals)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Metals and Alloys to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the physical properties of metals.
3. Practise this skill: describe the composition of alloys.
4. Practise this skill: identify the uses of metals and alloys in day-to-day life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Metals and Alloys from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Metals and Alloys: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Metals and Alloys?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are alloys important in day-to- day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Metals and Alloys means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the physical properties of metals.
5. Be able to: describe the composition of alloys.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
